subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What target-selection contract should native `/new` and `/reset` use in multi-agent channels, and what should happen when no target is explicit?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing between a native `agent:` option, `@agent` parsing, a selector prompt, or fail-closed behavior changes destructive command UX and security expectations.

options.title: Typed target selector
options.body: Add a native Discord `agent` selector or equivalent typed action and allow destructive resets only when the target is explicit or the existing route is unambiguous.

options.title: Mention parsing
options.body: Accept `@agent` text in command arguments, matching the report wording but with more transport-specific parsing risk.

options.title: Defer broad controls
options.body: Keep current routed-session behavior and leave multi-agent destructive command targeting to a larger command-targeting design.

recommendation.title: Typed target selector
recommendation.body: Add a native Discord `agent` selector or equivalent typed action and allow destructive resets only when the target is explicit or the existing route is unambiguous.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared native command session target helper introduced by steipete is the narrowest current seam for a cross-channel target contract.
